To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the total charge changing probability of relativistic nuclei is proportional to the square root of the beam charge and inversely proportional to the square of the target charge; the partial charge changing cross section for a particular fragment is proportional to the product of the beam and target charge; and the fission probability of relativistic gold nuclei is proportional to both the beam and target charges.

(1) The total charge-changing cross section for relativistic ions interacting with targets can be represented by a function that is a linear combination of two functions that are functions only of the charge of the projectile and the target.

the total charge-changing cross section is well described by the expression σ _{tot} = σ _{coul} [1 + 0.2(1 - Z _{T} /A _{T} ) ^{2} ], where σ _{coul is} the Coulomb barrier penetration cross section, Z _{T} and A _{T} are the charge and mass of the target nucleus.

the study of nuclear fragmentation and fission at relativistic energies, and we have developed simple representations of the charge changing and fission cross sections for use in the design of future relativistic heavy ion accelerators and in the interpretation of the results of future relativistic nuclear collisions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have a good understanding of the charge-changing processes in relativistic nuclear collisions, but there are still some unresolved questions.
the total and partial cross sections are well described in terms of the charge and energy dependence of a few parameters.

the systematics of the release and distribution of residual nuclei from the interaction of relativistic heavy nuclei are now known to a level of accuracy that permits their use in the design and interpretation of experiments in the relativistic heavy-ion program at the Bevalac.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it has established the systematic variation of the total and partial cross sections for the interaction of relativistic nuclei with targets of different charge.
we have shown that the charge changing process for heavy ions is a complex process involving many steps.
we have developed a systematics of the production of lighter nuclei from heavy ions at high energies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross sections for the emission of lighter nuclei are well represented by a single parameter, the total charge changing (TCC) cross section.
the charge changing cross section is a function of the charge and energy only, not of the mass number.
the cross sections for the charge changing of the projectile and the fission of the projectile can be described by simple expressions, which depend on the charge and the energy of the projectile.
